1) Goals we heard from ACME:
- 99th percentile tail latency target: 300ms for streaming chat use case (1-4 token batches).
- Sustained throughput target: ~1,500 requests/minute (peak 3k rpm) with up to 200 concurrent sessions.
- Must support streaming responses (chunked server-sent events) with sub-200ms first-byte goal from service if on the same VPC region.

2) Environment & constraints:
- ACME will evaluate Redwood Private deployed in their AWS VPC (single region, us-west-2) with option to test on-prem later.
- We discussed VPN peering vs AWS Transit Gateway; you mentioned procurement will want peering + site-to-site VPN for DR.

3) Action items / next steps:
- Marissa: share recommended SLOs and quantization/instance profile suggestions for our expected workload (Marissa to send by EOD today).
- ACME (Anna): share a network diagram and current egress/bandwidth limits; confirm whether peering or TGW is preferred for pilot.
- Jordan: set up a short tech validation call w/ Dev Patel and ACME infra to walk network and perf tests (propose Thu or Fri).

Attachments: will follow (Marissa will attach perf recs).

Thanks again — excited to keep momentum.

Thanks Jordan — adding a few technical clarifications and recommendations based on the targets you quoted:

Summary of recommended profiles for pilot:
- Instance profile: 2x A10G (or equivalent A100 40GB) per shard for low-latency streaming; start with 4 shards for capacity headroom to hit 1.5k rpm with 200 concurrencies.
- Quantization: fp16 inference for best latency/quality tradeoff; int8 quant could be evaluated for cost saves but expect ~10-15% latency variance.
- Batching: configure small max-batch sizes (8-16) with adaptive latency-aware batching to preserve PB99.

Networking & latency expectations:
- If Redwood Private deployed in your VPC with peering in us-west-2, we typically see intra-VPC p99 < 30ms for inference-only hop (network + runtime). First-byte for streaming typically ~40-60ms from service once model starts generating.
- With site-to-site VPN to on-prem, add conservative +40-80ms depending on hop and encryption; recommend test from your on-prem test client to a sample endpoint to measure RTT and jitter before pilot.

Perf validation plan:
- Step 1: Network validation (ACME provides diagram + run traceroutes/ping tests to our test endpoint).
- Step 2: Synthetic load test from ACME region to objective target (1.5k sustained rpm, spikes to 3k) using typical prompt distribution.
- Step 3: Streaming latency check (first-byte and median chunk times).

I attached a short PDF with SLO tuning recommendations and an example test harness we use for pilots (redwood-slo-recs.pdf).

Happy to jump on the tech call — Jordan, I can join Dev on whichever slot Anna prefers.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Anna — quick technical notes from our infra side: 

1) Peering vs TGW vs VPN:
- VPC peering is fine for the pilot and gives lowest hop count and latency; peering + site-to-site VPN as DR is a common setup. Transit Gateway is supported but adds routing complexity; we can work with your network/infra team on either.

2) MTU:
- MTU 9001 is fine; the only caveat is any interconnect that performs MSS clamping (we'll surface issues during the net tests).

3) Egress & bandwidth:
- For 3k rpm peak with 200 concurrencies and streaming payloads, 12 Gbps should be sufficient for short pilot tests, but if your requests include large context windows or heavy attachments you may need 15-20 Gbps headroom.

4) Ports & firewall:
- Streaming uses HTTPS (443) with long-lived HTTP/2 or SSE connections. Ensure outbound to our test endpoints on 443 and allow sustained concurrent connections from your staging IP range.

5) Latency budget breakdown (rough):
- Client <-> ACME staging cluster: depends on your infra (not on us).
- ACME staging -> VPC peering hop: typically 1-5ms.
- VPC inter-subnet + LB + inference runtime: ~25-60ms p99 depending on model and batching.
- Total p99 estimate (end-to-end): 60-200ms for intra-VPC; add 40-80ms for VPN/on-prem paths.

If you can share traceroute/ping and a sample request size/profile, we can provision a small test shard and run a synthetic pass to see where bottlenecks land.

I can make Thu 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 14:00-15:00 PT available for the tech call.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
